searchText: hello here, I'm a little confusing about the approaches for dev con vs public version, i think yesterday we briefly talked, but it seems didn't have final conclusion. here is the 2 approaches in visual explanation, I have the impression as we are building in approach #1, want to make sure everyone is on the same page. if too small for you, here is the link: https://www.figma.com/file/oRGtI6kDrhCBgfeuF6DyPg?node-id=284:511#259096923 the intent is that early contributions will still be valid, so i'd say #1 <@427491045308235776> or <@550420431744794624> should confirm though! yes, please 👆 <kevaundray> > <kevaundray> In #1 I interpret it as, the ceremony would be ongoing even after devcon with the mvp, so it doesn't stop until the public version is done (re @kzg_ceremony_bot: <Trent Van Epps> [reply]: the intent is that early contributions will still be valid, so i'd say #1) <kevaundray> Whereas I was under the impression that we wanted also to demo the ceremony ending and then contributors being able to verify that their contribution was included. The previous contributions can then be preserved by restarting from where the MVP left off in a few months <kevaundray> You could still verify that your contribution was included in the most updated transcript and have the ceremony continue at dev con. Though we may want to advise people to not do this when the real ceremony starts or just not expose that endpoint in the public version, as we want to emphasise that you should verify that your contribution is included in the final transcript that everyone agrees to use, ie its a two step process apart of the approach, we will need to figure out some logistic as well, for ex: how do we plan to give out the code for mvp? if using approach #2, how do we plan to inform early contributor about the public release version and some instruction? 🤔 if i look at the plans, it does sounds like approach #2, <@550420431744794624> could you confirm with us? just want to make sure everyone is on same page 😅 🤓 🙏 <CarlBeek> no, there is no intention to demo the ceremony ending at devcon. imo it’s not worth the dev time and community confusion of ending something that we will be continuing anyway. <CarlBeek> i do want to extract an intermediate output transcript for client teams to have for testing, but i don’t want to give the impression that anything is final <CarlBeek> i’ve already had several people reach out to me worried that they missed the contribution or some kind of sign up process. there is lots of confusion out there already <trent_vanepps> > <trent_vanepps> same - other than having a mailing list, we can just tell people to keep an eye out, it will be very public for a few months (re @CarlBeek: i’ve already had several people reach out to me worried that they missed the contribution or some kind of sign up process. there is lots of confusion out there already) <kevaundray> > <kevaundray> This is a fair point, re confusion. Its still beneficial to show the act of the verifying your contribution in the demo, though as mentioned above, this may also lead to confusion since in the public version, you verify once the ceremony has completed (re @CarlBeek: no, there is no intention to demo the ceremony ending at devcon. imo it’s not worth the dev time and community confusion of ending something that we will be continuing anyway.) <CarlBeek> i don’t want this to be a demo, i’d like to make it the start of the actual ceremony <trent_vanepps> > <trent_vanepps> right, that was my assumption as well. the only "demo" characteristics is that it's gated. but the gated output should be folded into the public portion (re @CarlBeek: i don’t want this to be a demo, i’d like to make it the start of the actual ceremony) <trent_vanepps> we could point people towards the protocol support google group? i think there's a good reason to announce there - that way we can have people sign up in advance <kevaundray> > <kevaundray> Ah okay, I was under the wrong assumption. Then the UI will not need to show verification if its just to showcase the start of the ceremony (re @trent_vanepps: right, that was my assumption as well. the only "demo" characteristics is that it's gated. but the gated output should be folded into the public portion) <CarlBeek> it’s mostly about drawing attention to the ceremony itself and how “easy” it is to participate thank you guys~~ so the approach we are taking is #1, this is very helpful for me, I will continue to mock up the UI🙏
